newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. Wilson signs $67 billion budget.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. Wilson signs $67 billion budget.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson signed the state's $67 billion budget Monday but used his line-item veto power to axe an unspecified amount in spending measures, officials said.
The budget was signed 49 days into the state's fiscal year, which began July 1. The legislature passed the budget bill last week after the second-longest budget deadlock in the state's history.

A spokesman for the state treasurer said staff members were calculating the exact dollar amount of spending measures vetoed by Wilson. The spokesman said his office would release the figure later Monday morning.

Wilson, a Republican, said last week that he would veto parts of the budget to pressure Democrats who control the legislature to pass an education bill he supports. The bill would allow students in public schools to to be given an assessment test.
Wilson wants a single statewide assessment test in English only, while Democrats want students who are not proficient in English to be able to take the test in their native language.
The main beneficiary of the budget is education, whose funding will be raised to an all-time high. The budget includes $100 million in funding for local police.

Passage of the budget was held up by disputes over welfare reform. When Wilson's plan for a $1 billion income tax cut was blocked by Democrats, Wilson last month ordered the state to repay $1.2 billion to the state retirement system to settle a court case. The decision forced legislators to cut spending.
